tasks.short: Calculate statistical measures and examine results using agreed formulas.

steps.what: Load the validated dataset into the calculation workbook.
Check the study brief and confirm formulas, populations, and exclusions.
Apply formulas and calculate summaries, ratios, and statistical measures.
Examine unusual results and record limitations or questions.
Save the results, specification, and finding notes for reporting.

tasks.design: A versioned calculation job in the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads the validated dataset and approved specification, then produces results and diagnostic plots. A configured flow files the analysis package in the {DOCS}; the assistant examines flagged results, and the statistical analyst approves changed methods before use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workbook formulas, dataset versions, and method notes were maintained separately. Connecting them and testing repeatable calculations required development time.
tasks.enabler_now: Established statistical libraries and scheduled jobs already support this work. AI coding can shorten connector and test development; numerical validity still depends on specifications and checks.
tasks.still_hard: Population definitions, missing-data treatment, and unusual distributions require statistical judgement. Actuarial assumptions need qualified oversight.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a correct calculation answers the wrong question, and explain uncertainty to the analyst.

ambition.what: Weekly escalation of emerging cost variation to the budget analyst.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rerunning formulas to examining unusual results and preparing decision evidence. The assistant can prioritise investigation requests within agreed thresholds; method approval stays with the statistical analyst.

reach.task: Investigate cost variance against forecast.
reach.learn: Forecast assumptions, cost drivers, and materiality thresholds.

reach.task: Prepare sensitivity analysis for risk assumptions.
reach.learn: Scenario design, uncertainty measures, and limits of statistical inference.

evidence.claim: Versioned deterministic calculations can replace repeated application of agreed statistical formulas.
The proposed time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are estimates, not measured outcomes.

The dataset has passed source validation before calculation.
A statistical analyst approves methods; an actuary approves actuarial assumptions where applicable.

tasks.short: Load compiled observations into analysis tools and correct rejected records.

steps.what: Inspect the compiled dataset and field instructions stored in the {DOCS}.
Arrange columns and codes to match the analysis tool using the {SPREADSHEET}.
Type or paste observations into the statistics application {OTHER}.
Run validation and compare record counts in the statistics application {OTHER}.
Check rejected observations against source material and record justified corrections.
Reload corrected records and confirm acceptance in the statistics application {OTHER}.

tasks.design: A versioned mapping on the {DATA_PLATFORM} converts the compiled dataset into the import format for the statistics application {OTHER}, removing retyping. Configured import checks reconcile counts, identifiers and totals before records become available for analysis. The {WORKFLOW} routes rejected records to a person and reloads logged corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different field layouts and weak import checks made manual entry seem safer. Schema changes broke informal transfer routines.
tasks.enabler_now: Native batch imports often already exist. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of adapters, reconciliation and useful rejection messages.
tasks.still_hard: A valid field can still contain the wrong observation or meaning. GDPR requires appropriate access and retention; EU AI Act and national consultation requirements depend on the actual deployment.
tasks.human_edge: Determine the intended observation without silently changing source facts to satisfy validation.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less retyping and more targeted correction. No new decision rights arise from faster data loading.

reach.task: Reconcile financial reporting inputs to source records.
reach.learn: Control totals, correction evidence and audit trails.

evidence.claim: Native imports, field mapping and deterministic validation can remove routine retyping without a model.
The documented UK spreadsheet failure supports checking complete record transfer rather than trusting a successful import message.

Who may correct observations and what evidence is required.

tasks.statement: Enter data into computers for use in analyses or reports.

tasks.short: Collect source records, resolve gaps and compile statistical datasets and summaries.

steps.what: Export sales, production and workforce records from source systems.
Read source forms and transcribe observations into a {SPREADSHEET}.

loop.input: Residual scanned or variable-layout source forms and a fixed field schema.
loop.output: Form dataset with field-level source references and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Check required fields, types, ranges, identifiers and source totals; review extracted observations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per form; unreadable or unresolved fields go to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured forms use direct imports; residual scans and variable layouts lack reliable field positions.

steps.what: Merge records and standardise dates, units and categories in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Compare coverage and totals with the source register and study specification.
Ask data owners to resolve missing or conflicting observations through the {EMAIL}.
Apply corrections and calculate specified statistical summaries in the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Scheduled exports from the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HCM} feed a governed pipeline on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Code lists and deterministic checks standardise records and calculate approved formulas; a bounded loop extracts residual forms for review. An exception queue in the {WORKFLOW} records source-owner corrections before the pipeline releases compiled datasets.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source formats, identifiers and units differed. Missing observations required coordination, and compilation rules often lived in individual workbooks.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduled exports can supply structured records. AI-assisted coding makes mappings, checks and an exception queue cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Source owners must explain missing data and definition changes. GDPR limits workforce-data use; national rules may require employee consultation, and EU AI Act applicability needs assessment for the actual use.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparently comparable records measure different things and obtain a defensible correction.

ambition.what: Review emerging departmental cost variances weekly using complete source coverage.

tasks.altitude: Routine collection and compilation shrink, leaving more time to investigate coverage and definition changes. The assistant can recommend withholding unreliable summaries; finance retains business decisions.

reach.learn: Cost drivers, budget hierarchies and materiality thresholds.

The ONS occupation-coding case demonstrates rules-first coding with models for additional coverage; its results do not establish finance accuracy.
Source reconciliation and specified statistical formulas can run deterministically.

The study specification defines populations, units, categories and formulas.

tasks.statement: Compile statistics from source materials, such as production or sales records, quality-control or test records, time sheets, or survey sheets.

tasks.short: Produce charts and reports that explain statistical findings.

steps.what: Select the analysis package and confirm the report period and audience.
Build tables and charts with suitable scales, labels, and comparisons.
Write descriptions of findings and assemble charts into the report.

loop.input: Verified analysis results, finding notes, report brief, and approved report template.
loop.output: Draft descriptive paragraphs linked to result identifiers, with unresolved questions marked.
loop.check: Validate every numerical claim against results; require source references and review unsupported interpretations.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section within a fixed token budget; use tables and approved captions if checks fail.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle recurring captions, but variable findings need readable prose. The loop drafts descriptions without choosing methods or asserting causes.

steps.what: Review interpretations, limitations, chart choices, and suitability for the intended audience.
File the approved report and send its link to authorised recipients.

tasks.design: Configured charts in the {BI} read versioned results from the {DATA_PLATFORM}, while a template generator assembles the report in the {DOCS}. A bounded model drafts variable descriptions from verified findings; deterministic checks link claims to results, and the statistical analyst approves the report before a configured {WORKFLOW} files it and sends an internal link through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts, figures, and narrative were copied between files, making updates fragile. Templates covered layout but could not describe changing findings.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured charts and document templates already support repeatable assembly. Bounded drafting can reduce writing effort when every claim remains linked to approved evidence.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible explanation can exceed what the data supports. Small groups, uncertainty, and misleading scales require careful review.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what the audience needs to understand and distinguish description, association, and defensible explanation.

ambition.what: A monthly cost-driver briefing for department budget owners.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more of the week shaping explanations and checking evidence, with less chart formatting. They can propose the briefing agenda; the statistical analyst retains approval of interpretations and release.

reach.task: Prepare a management briefing on cost drivers.
reach.learn: Decision context, materiality, and concise explanation of uncertainty.

reach.task: Design reusable finance reporting views.
reach.learn: Accessible chart design, aggregation choices, and disclosure controls.

evidence.claim: Configured charts and data-driven document templates can automate recurring report assembly.
CHILI GraFx supports governed layout templates; this is capability evidence, not a statistical-reporting case.
Bounded drafting needs numerical grounding and human review of interpretation; no digest case measures this workflow.

assumptions: The analysis package contains verified results and explicit limitations.
Routine chart types and report structures can be configured in existing systems.
Reports are distributed internally to an approved recipient list.
Static captions use templates; the model handles only variable descriptive prose.
GDPR applies to personal data, including small-group disclosure risks; EU AI Act obligations depend on intended use.
Build ranges include access review and consultation under national rules where applicable.
The reporting build reuses the calculation and dataset foundation.

Maintain chart specifications and report templates.
Check recipient permissions and small-group disclosures.
Monitor drafting quality after model or prompt changes.
tasks.statement: Compile reports, charts, or graphs that describe and interpret findings of analyses.

tasks.short: Check source data, resolve discrepancies, and release a validated dataset.

steps.what: Open source extracts and confirm the expected period, files, and populations.
Reconcile record counts and financial totals against independent source controls.
Check missing fields, duplicates, valid codes, ranges, and cross-field consistency.
Assess unusual values against prior periods and documented business changes.
Send specific discrepancy questions and correction requests to the source owner.
Investigate discrepancies and provide corrected records or an explanation.
Recheck corrections, document exceptions, and approve the dataset for analysis.

tasks.design: A deterministic validation job in the {DATA_PLATFORM} compares registered datasets with source manifests, control totals from the {ERP}, and versioned validation rules. A configured queue in the {WORKFLOW} prepares correction requests through the {EMAIL}; people assess contextual exceptions and source corrections before the rechecked dataset is released for analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checks were embedded in separate workbooks, and source totals were not consistently captured. Automatic flags could identify discrepancies but could not supply missing facts.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable checks, independent control totals, and tracked correction queues are established techniques. AI coding can make their implementation cheaper without changing the need for source-owner investigation.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible value can still be wrong, and a missing record may leave no visible gap. Independent controls and business knowledge remain essential.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish genuine business changes from errors and obtain evidence from the person responsible for the source.

ambition.what: A pre-close data readiness check for the finance team.

tasks.altitude: The assistant focuses on unexplained differences and release readiness instead of inspecting every field. They can hold a dataset that fails agreed checks and release one within delegated tolerances; material unresolved exceptions go to the statistical analyst.

reach.task: Reconcile period-close balances and supporting records.
reach.learn: Independent control totals, cut-off rules, and reconciliation evidence.

reach.task: Evaluate the reliability of financial data controls.
reach.learn: Control design, sampling limits, and evidence of completeness.

evidence.claim: Deterministic checks can detect missing fields, invalid codes, duplicates, and reconciliation differences.
A documented public-health incident lost 15,841 cases through a spreadsheet row limit, supporting explicit completeness checks.
Automatic validation cannot establish source truth without independent controls or source-owner evidence.

Independent source counts or totals can be obtained.
The assistant has delegated dataset-release tolerances; material unresolved exceptions require analyst approval.
Record maintenance handles schema and update conflicts; this task establishes analytical completeness and plausibility.

tasks.short: Prepare, check and publish statistical tables, charts and explanations.

steps.what: Retrieve approved analysis results from the {BI}.
Assemble tables and charts in a report stored in the {DOCS}.
Write explanations and limitations alongside the tables.

loop.input: Approved analysis results, method notes and publication brief.
loop.output: Report narrative with references to supplied tables and method notes.
loop.check: Verify every number against supplied results; a person checks interpretation and caveats.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unresolved claims return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed captions cannot explain unusual results and changing study limitations.

steps.what: Check report figures against the {SPREADSHEET} and review disclosure risks.
Review the checked report and approve its release through the {EMAIL}.
Publish the approved report through the {CMS}.

tasks.design: A generator combines approved {BI} results with governed templates in the {DOCS}; a bounded loop drafts explanations from supplied evidence. Deterministic checks compare figures and flag disclosure issues, while people approve interpretation and release. The {WORKFLOW} publishes the approved version through the {CMS} and records its provenance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report assembly crossed exports, document templates and release approvals. Changing commentary prevented complete template coverage.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing export and approval features cover much of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building template and validation glue.
tasks.still_hard: Misleading comparisons, disclosure through small groups and late revisions still need judgement. GDPR applies to personal data; applicable EU AI Act duties depend on the use.
tasks.human_edge: Explain what a result supports, what it leaves uncertain and how readers might misinterpret it.

ambition.what: An accessible statistical release with plain-language explanations for department budget owners.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from report assembly to interpretation and release quality. The assistant can recommend clearer comparisons; release authority stays with the finance manager.

reach.learn: Accessible chart design, semantic measures and refresh dependencies.

evidence.claim: Governed templates can automate layout assembly; CHILI GraFx provides this capability.
A UK case documents records lost through a spreadsheet row limit, supporting explicit completeness checks.
Statistical narrative and disclosure review still require people; the proposed combined workflow is a design estimate.

tasks.short: Agree with clients how statistical findings should be presented and used.

steps.what: Read the client's presentation request and record its audience and deadline.
Prepare example charts and relevant definitions from the {DOCS} and {BI}.
Discuss intended decisions, audience needs, chart choices and limitations with the client.

loop.stop: One draft and one repair; unclear requirements return to the client conversation.

tasks.previous_blocker: Client needs emerge through discussion and negotiation. Preparation and follow-up were bundled into the same manual service.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake and reusable chart examples already support preparation. A bounded drafting loop can organise notes while leaving commitments to people.
tasks.still_hard: Clients may ask for a persuasive chart that the evidence cannot support. Confidentiality, GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties need attention; national rules govern any employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Uncover the real decision, challenge misleading framing and negotiate a useful, honest presentation.

tasks.short: Assign approved statistical codes to responses before loading the analysis dataset.

steps.what: Read coding instructions and select the applicable codebook version.
Match clear responses to listed codes in the coding workbook.
Interpret ambiguous responses and record justified coding decisions.

loop.input: Unmatched response text and the applicable codebook entries.
loop.output: An allowed code proposal with source wording and rationale, or an abstention.
loop.check: Validate code membership and version; the assistant checks meaning before acceptance.
loop.stop: One proposal per response, with one retry for invalid output; unresolved cases go to the study lead.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact matches and approved synonyms run first. Remaining descriptions require interpretation of free text.

steps.what: Validate code ranges and totals, then export the coded dataset.

tasks.design: A versioned codebook in the {DOCS} drives deterministic mappings on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with constrained choices offered at collection where possible. A bounded model proposes codes only for unmatched text in a {WORKFLOW} review queue. Validated records feed statistical analysis software in the {OTHER}, with unresolved entries explicitly marked.
tasks.previous_blocker: Codebooks changed between studies, and free-text descriptions resisted simple lookups. Workbook mappings often lacked tests and version history.
tasks.enabler_now: Small mapping services and validation checks are easier to build. Bounded text classification can assist with the residual cases without controlling the codebook.
tasks.still_hard: Rare categories, changing definitions and systematic miscoding require expert review. A plausible code is not proof of correct classification.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding when a response does not fit the classification and when a coding choice would distort the study.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on emerging coding ambiguity

tasks.altitude: Routine lookup work gives way to reviewing ambiguous categories and checking coding quality. The assistant can correct mappings within approved definitions; new categories and definition changes stay with the study lead.

Versioned codebooks, allowed-value checks and reconciliation totals support deterministic coding and controlled exports.

assumptions: An approved codebook exists and most responses have stable mappings.
The study specification explicitly identifies the codebook version.
The final step uses statistical analysis software, represented by the {OTHER}.
Coding supports aggregate analysis rather than decisions about individual eligibility or employment.
unknowns: What share of responses can approved mappings code correctly?
Who can approve ambiguous codes and changes to definitions?
Is there a representative, independently reviewed coding sample?
Which personal data and access or consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can constrained collection fields remove common coding work upstream?
Does a bounded classifier improve reviewed throughput after deterministic mapping?
Which categories need stricter sampling because errors would bias conclusions?
new_work: Review proposed codes and investigate abstentions.
Maintain codebook versions and approved synonyms.
Sample automatic mappings and monitor category-level error patterns.
Retest mappings and model proposals when definitions change.
tasks.statement: Code data prior to computer entry, using lists of codes.

tasks.short: Check survey responses for recording defects and separate unusable responses while preserving an audit trail.

steps.what: Collect returned forms and register the response batch.
Check whether paper responses use the required marking medium.
Check recorded answers for missing fields, invalid values and contradictory combinations.
Inspect ambiguous responses and decide whether they can be used.

loop.input: Flagged response, original scan or electronic answer, and approved usability rules.
loop.output: Suggested defect category and disposition with the relevant source passage.
loop.check: A person compares the suggestion with the original and approves usability; unclear answers remain unresolved.
loop.stop: One classification attempt per flagged response; illegible or conflicting evidence goes directly to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Field rules handle structured defects, but handwriting and free-text contradictions require reading the original.

steps.what: File usable responses and set aside unusable forms with their rejection reasons.

tasks.design: Validated survey forms in the {WORKFLOW} prevent routine recording defects and register responses automatically. Readable paper submissions are scanned into the {DOCS}; rules flag defects, and a bounded model assists with ambiguous text for human disposition. A response register on the {WORKFLOW} preserves originals, accepted records and quarantine reasons without deleting responses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper capture requirements made physical inspection necessary. Checks and rejection reasons were disconnected from the analysis dataset.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic forms and readable scanning can remove obsolete pen-versus-pencil restrictions. Configured validation and a small exception queue handle most remaining checks.
tasks.still_hard: Illegible handwriting, accessibility needs and contradictory answers persist. Exclusion can distort the sample even when each rejection follows a rule.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a recording defect from a valid unusual answer and protecting respondents whose access needs differ.

ambition.what: A survey-quality report showing exclusion reasons and their effect on the sample.

tasks.altitude: The week moves from inspecting every form to resolving ambiguity and reviewing exclusion patterns. The assistant gains authority to request clarification within the survey protocol; changing eligibility rules needs the survey lead.

reach.task: Assess missingness and selection bias.
reach.learn: Missing-data mechanisms, exclusion sensitivity and sample representativeness.

reach.task: Review collection and retention of personal survey data.
reach.learn: Purpose limitation, access controls, retention and respondent rights under GDPR.

evidence.claim: Scanning services can turn business forms into data; this supports intake, not automatic usability decisions.
A documented occupation-coding case combines rules and tested models; transfer to survey defect classification requires local validation.
A documented row-limit failure supports checking record counts and avoiding uncontrolled workbook accumulation.

assumptions: This supplemental task describes a remaining paper-heavy survey process; other surveys may already be electronic.
The marking-medium check exists for capture compatibility, rather than a mandatory survey protocol.
Replacement capture accepts readable pen and pencil marks, allowing that check to disappear.
Accessible paper intake remains available, with occasional physical handling included as exception work.
Rules flag defects; ambiguous exclusions require approval and originals remain recoverable.
Consultation ranges include applicable employee consultation under national rules; this is not a per-worker speed dashboard.
unknowns: Actual electronic and paper response shares.
Whether the survey protocol mandates a marking medium.
Scan quality and prevalence of handwriting.
Approved usability criteria and clarification permissions.
Personal data categories, retention periods and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which defects can be prevented without forcing respondents to supply inappropriate answers?
Does quarantine disproportionately remove any respondent group?
How accurately can the loop classify local scans without inventing answers?
Can batch counts reconcile intake, accepted responses and quarantine?
new_work: Review ambiguous responses against originals.
Handle accessible paper submissions and failed scans.
Maintain validation rules and classification examples.
Monitor exclusion patterns and reconcile response counts.
Maintain access controls and retention schedules.
tasks.statement: Check survey responses for errors, such as the use of pens instead of pencils, and set aside response forms that cannot be used.

tasks.short: Interview respondents and maintain accurate, usable records of their answers.

steps.what: Arrange an interview time with the respondent.
Prepare the approved question guide and relevant respondent context.
Ask questions, clarify meaning and capture the respondent's answers.
Transfer answers from interview notes into the response register.
Check unclear answers, record limitations and mark responses ready for analysis.

tasks.design: Configure scheduling in the {CALENDAR} and generate interview guides from approved material in the {DOCS}. During the human interview, a structured form in the {WORKFLOW} stores answers directly in the response register, removing later re-entry. Required-field checks flag gaps; the assistant resolves meaning and releases responses for analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Interview notes and analysis registers used different formats. Respondent-specific preparation and subsequent copying consumed time between infrequent interviews.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured forms, template generation and scheduling are established capabilities that can be connected cheaply. This design needs no model or recording.
tasks.still_hard: Rapport, neutral probing, sensitive disclosures and contradictory answers remain human work. Structured capture must not disrupt listening.
tasks.human_edge: Earning candid answers, noticing hesitation and clarifying meaning without leading the respondent.

ambition.what: Short follow-up interviews on unexplained budget variances

tasks.altitude: Interview time remains human, while preparation and re-entry shrink. The assistant can select follow-up questions within the approved protocol and document uncertainty; conclusions about budgets remain with the budget analyst.

reach.task: Investigate explanations for unusual departmental spending.
reach.learn: Variance analysis, neutral questioning and the distinction between reported explanations and verified evidence.

evidence.claim: Structured capture during an interview can remove later re-entry while preserving free-text answers.
Scheduling and approved-guide generation can be automated independently of the human conversation.

assumptions: Interviews follow an approved protocol and allow direct digital note-taking.
The interview list already authorizes routine scheduling contact.
Appointments and messages contain minimal study detail.
Recording and automatic transcription are outside the proposed design.
Unlike the high disappearance prior, conversation remains substantial because clarification and trust are central.
unknowns: Can interviewers capture answers directly without harming rapport or accessibility?
Which questions involve personal or sensitive information?
What GDPR basis, access restrictions and retention periods apply?
Do national rules require employee consultation or works-council involvement?
Who approves changes to the interview protocol?
research_questions: Which fields can be captured during the interview without distracting the interviewer?
Does a pilot preserve answer completeness and respondent comfort?
Which contradictions require respondent follow-up rather than an internal correction?
Does the intended use trigger obligations under the EU AI Act if model features are later added?
new_work: Maintain interview guides and response-field definitions.
Review missing fields and preserve explicit uncertainty.
Handle scheduling exceptions and accessibility needs.
Check that direct capture preserves respondents' meaning.
tasks.statement: Interview people and keep track of their responses.

tasks.short: Prepare survey recipients, release invitations and track delivery and responses.

steps.what: Compile eligible recipients and check addresses against the study scope.
Prepare the questionnaire link, invitation text and return instructions.
Approve recipients, invitation wording, timing and reminder limits.
Send survey invitations and record the release.
Check delivery failures and response status, then send permitted reminders.

tasks.design: Configure questionnaire templates, delivery tracking and reminder limits in survey software represented by the {OTHER}. A deterministic connection to the {ERP} prepares eligible recipients, while the {WORKFLOW} records release approval before invitations leave through the {EMAIL}. Delivery exceptions enter a review queue, and response status suppresses unnecessary reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recipient exports, survey settings and delivery records were disconnected. Staff manually checked scope and copied approval details between tools.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing survey configuration can handle most distribution. Small integrations can connect approved lists, release records and response status without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Contact eligibility, accessibility, anonymity and persistent nonresponse need human decisions. Sending more reminders does not establish representative coverage.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing appropriate contact methods and recognizing when outreach would pressure respondents or bias the sample.
tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer list transfers and manual sends, with more time for delivery exceptions and coverage gaps. The assistant can resolve routine delivery issues within the approved plan; recipient scope and reminder limits remain with the study lead.

reach.task: Collect structured assumptions from cost-centre owners for a forecast.
reach.learn: Sampling coverage, response deadlines and how missing assumptions affect the forecast.

evidence.claim: Survey software commonly supports invitation templates, response tracking and scheduled reminders.
Recipient validation and approval-bound dispatch can use deterministic rules without a model.

assumptions: The study lead supplies an approved questionnaire; questionnaire design is outside this task.
Supplier or business-contact details are available from the {ERP}.
Survey software is represented by the {OTHER}.
The current process includes external recipients; employee surveys may use different source records.
Approval time is included in task elapsed effort across participating roles.
The release approval covers the exact initial batch; the assistant reviews reminder batches within its approved limits.
unknowns: Does the survey tool already support all required distribution controls?
What lawful basis, notices, retention and contact restrictions apply under GDPR?
Does the study require anonymous responses or identifiable follow-up?
Which national rules require employee consultation or works-council involvement?
Which recipients require accessible or offline alternatives?
research_questions: Can the existing survey tool replace the recipient workbook?
Can response tracking suppress reminders without exposing confidential answers?
Which contact methods improve coverage among small suppliers?
new_work: Review recipient exceptions and approve release batches.
Handle delivery failures and requests for alternative response methods.
Maintain templates, suppression rules and reminder limits.
Check access, retention and response-status synchronization.

tasks.short: Write and maintain code that prepares finance data and runs approved statistical analyses.

steps.what: Translate the analysis request and approved methods into calculation requirements.
Adapt existing import routines, calculation functions and output templates.
Write custom transformations and calculations beyond the existing library.

loop.input: Calculation specification, approved functions, code scaffold and synthetic test dataset.
loop.check: Run in an isolated environment; check dependencies, reference calculations, edge cases and data access.
loop.stop: At most two generation-and-repair passes per change; failed checks return to manual coding.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reusable templates cover standard routines, but new transformations require translating written requirements into code.

steps.what: Test calculations against reference results and approve the code for use.
Save the approved version and update its run instructions.

tasks.design: A generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles approved routines from the method plan and data dictionary. A bounded model drafts only uncovered code, while deterministic tests and an analysis lead's approval control release. The {DOCS} receives versioned run instructions and validation records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements, reusable code and reference calculations were scattered. Automating a new calculation still required bespoke development.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can reduce implementation effort. Reusable routines, isolated execution and automated checks make generated code reviewable.
tasks.still_hard: Correct syntax does not establish statistical validity. Missing data, changing definitions and independent reference results still require expertise.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a calculation faithfully implements the specification but answers the wrong business question.

ambition.what: A reusable sensitivity-analysis service for budget analysts.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated coding to specification, validation and unusual calculations. With delegated authority, the assistant can accept routine implementation changes within approved methods; method changes still need the analysis lead.

reach.task: Build reproducible analytical pipelines.
reach.learn: Version control, automated testing, dependency management and reproducibility.

reach.task: Compare financial scenarios.
reach.learn: Scenario assumptions, forecast drivers and sensitivity interpretation.

evidence.claim: Reusable statistical routines and automated reference checks support deterministic code generation and validation.
A bounded coding model can draft bespoke routines, but independent checks and human release approval remain necessary.

assumptions: The assistant writes small analytical routines rather than production financial decision engines.
Approved methods and reusable functions exist for a meaningful share of requests.
Build ranges cover one initial analysis family and accessible data sources.
The coding loop uses synthetic or authorised data and approved processing arrangements under GDPR.
unknowns: Current coding environment and reusable library coverage.
Availability of independently verified reference calculations.
Who can approve code and change analytical methods.
Access lead times and applicable consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which recurring routines can be generated entirely from parameters?
Which defects escape current reference checks?
How much coding time concerns genuinely new transformations?
new_work: Review generated changes and investigate failed checks.
Maintain reusable routines and independent reference datasets.
Update permissions, dependencies and release records.
Check that model-generated tests do not merely repeat the code's assumptions.

tasks.short: Prepare and explain statistical findings to finance stakeholders, then record agreed actions.

steps.what: Gather validated results, definitions and caveats for the stakeholder audience.
Build charts and tables with suitable scales, labels and uncertainty.
Write the explanation, key findings and limitations around the charts.

loop.input: Validated findings, chart pack, method limitations and audience brief.
loop.output: Draft briefing with references to supplied findings.
loop.check: Check every number against source results; a reviewer checks uncertainty, unsupported claims and causal language.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims are removed or rewritten by a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout, but explanations must connect varied findings to the audience's questions.

steps.what: Approve the briefing's interpretation and permitted audience.
Present findings, answer questions and clarify the implications with stakeholders.
Circulate the agreed actions and register unanswered questions.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} supplies validated findings to governed chart and briefing templates in the {DOCS}. A bounded model drafts explanations, and the analysis lead approves interpretation and audience before use. The assistant leads the discussion, while the {WORKFLOW} creates reviewed action records in the {PROJECT} and sends internal updates through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results, charts and explanations were assembled separately. Reusing an old briefing risked carrying forward stale numbers or caveats.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic chart generation and source-linked templates are established techniques. Bounded drafting can reduce writing time when findings are already validated.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders may misunderstand uncertainty or press for conclusions beyond the evidence. Sensitive findings and external publication need appropriate release judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the room, explaining uncomfortable findings and responding honestly when the evidence does not settle a question.

ambition.what: Monthly statistical briefings for operational budget owners.

tasks.altitude: Preparation takes less of the week, leaving more time for discussion and follow-up analysis. The assistant can prioritise clarification requests within an agreed remit; financial decisions remain with stakeholders.

reach.task: Use analysis to choose corrective financial actions.
reach.learn: Decision thresholds, materiality and how uncertainty affects action.

reach.task: Design stakeholder reporting.
reach.learn: Chart selection, accessible presentation and metric definitions.

evidence.claim: Governed templates can generate layouts from supplied content; this supports the layout block, not statistical interpretation.
Validated data can drive charts and briefing tables without a model loop.
Human discussion remains important even when preparation and follow-up paperwork are automated.

assumptions: The initial audience is internal finance stakeholders.
Results have passed validation before presentation preparation starts.
Agreed actions are captured in structured fields during the discussion.
The live conversation remains human; automation estimates concern its preparation and paperwork.
unknowns: Which briefings require external publication approval.
Current chart standards and accessibility requirements.
Permitted audiences for confidential results.
Who has authority to assign follow-up work.
research_questions: Which recurring stakeholder questions should become standard briefing fields?
Which chart choices have caused misunderstandings?
Can every published number be traced to a validated result?
new_work: Review drafted explanations and source references.
Maintain chart and briefing templates.
Handle requests that exceed the evidence or approved audience.
Review action records before circulation.
tasks.statement: Present results of statistical analyses to stakeholders.

role_batches.altitude: The role moves toward maintaining reliable study inputs, investigating exceptions, and preparing clear decision evidence. Dataset holds and routine release rights can be delegated; statistical methods, material exceptions, and consequential interpretations retain qualified approval.
reach: Budget analyst: investigate cost drivers and forecast deviations.
Accountant: reconcile reported figures to independent source controls.
Business intelligence analyst: maintain reusable datasets and reporting views.
Financial risk specialist: prepare sensitivity evidence for approved assumptions.

Data lineage and reconciliation
Versioned calculation and validation specifications
Accessible charts and evidence-based explanation
Exception investigation with source owners
Personal-data access and disclosure controls

Earn delegated authority to prioritise investigations and release routine datasets through demonstrated control quality.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts from collecting, retyping and assembling figures toward source quality, interpretation and presentation advice. Finance managers retain release and financial decision authority unless the customer explicitly delegates it.
reach: Budget Analysts: investigate cost variances and define decision-focused presentations.
Business Intelligence Analysts: build reusable measures and accessible reporting views.
Accountants and Auditors: reconcile reporting inputs and preserve correction evidence.

Deterministic validation, reconciliation and dataset versioning.
Accessible charts and plain-language statistical explanations.
Client discovery and scope negotiation.
GDPR-aware data handling and assessment of applicable EU AI Act and national rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A statistical reporting adviser who offers accessible releases and chart-selection clinics, helping budget owners interpret reliable figures before making decisions.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward analytical quality, exception handling and explaining uncertainty. Delegated rights can cover routine implementation changes and clarification requests; new methods, eligibility changes and financial decisions remain with their accountable leads.
reach: Data scientist: reproducible pipelines, statistical design and missing-data analysis.
Budget analyst: scenario comparisons and forecast assumptions.
Financial risk specialist: validation, dependence and uncertainty.
Business intelligence analyst: accessible reporting and metric definitions.
skills_to_grow: Independent reference testing and reproducible analysis.
Study design, statistical assumptions and selection bias.
Data lineage, access control and GDPR-aware handling.
Clear explanations of uncertainty and limits.
Review of generated code and source-grounded drafts.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A small analytical support service that delivers reproducible finance comparisons, survey-quality reports and sensitivity analyses, with explicit method approval and traceable results.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward study operations, data quality and targeted follow-up. The assistant gains limited authority to resolve routine document and coding exceptions within approved specifications; study design, statistical methods and financial conclusions remain with qualified owners.
reach: Support business intelligence analysts with versioned classifications and traceable datasets.
Support accountants with indexed control evidence.
Support budget analysts with structured assumption collection and variance interviews.
skills_to_grow: Reference-data management and codebook versioning
Data reconciliation and representative quality sampling
Survey coverage and nonresponse assessment
Neutral interviewing and uncertainty documentation
Access control, GDPR and applicable national rules
Configuration and maintenance of small data workflows
